params.body:
## Why

The job "Dependencies carry no new advisory" went red on #962 (and will on every pull request from now on): `source-map-js` 1.2.1 got a high advisory today ([GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q)), so `npm audit` counts 8 high packages against a ceiling of 7. Nothing in #962 touches dependencies.

## What

- `source-map-js` 1.2.1 → 1.2.2 (under PostCSS and jsdom): fixes the new advisory.
- `http-cache-semantics` 4.2.0 → 4.3.0 (under ably → got → cacheable-request): the workflow comment said "no fixed release yet"; 4.3.0 is that release ([GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp)).
- Ceiling 7 → 6 and the comment above the job updated.

Only those two entries in `package-lock.json` change (version, resolved, integrity); neither version adds a dependency. A plain `npm update` with the local npm also pruned the optional sass/terser entries, so the bump was made by hand to keep the diff to what it says.

## Checked

`npm ci`, `node .github/scripts/npm-audit-ceiling.mjs 6` (6, passes), `npm run build`, `vitest` (103 passed), `eslint` (0 errors).

After merging, re-run the failed audit job on #962: it audits the merge ref, so it picks up this lock file.
params.title: npm advisories back under the ceiling: 8 to 6
